title: Penn State closes on a 14–4 run after Hubbard’s dunk puts Mississippi State up five
excerpt: Penn State beat the Bulldogs 68–63 in the Bahamas. Mississippi State returns to Starkville to play Georgia Tech on Wednesday.
locality: Starkville, Mississippi, and Paradise Island, Bahamas.

paragraphs.text: With 6:34 left Friday night, Josh Hubbard took the ball away from Penn State’s Dasonte Bowen. Four seconds later, Hubbard dunked to put Mississippi State ahead 59–54. It was the Bulldogs’ last field goal. Penn State scored 14 of the last 18 points to win 68–63 in the Battle 4 Atlantis finale on Paradise Island in the Bahamas.

Mississippi State took a 36–29 lead into halftime and led by as many as 16 in the second half. Penn State caught the Bulldogs at 54 on a basket by Bowen. State scored the next five points, capped by Hubbard’s dunk. Brant Byers answered with a three for Penn State, and Bowen tied the game again before Byers put the Nittany Lions ahead at the foul line.

The score was 66–61 with eight seconds left. Kimani Hamilton hit two free throws for Mississippi State to cut the gap to three. Byers made both of his free throws with six seconds to go, and Bowen stole the ball on the Bulldogs’ final possession. Penn State won the second half 39–27.

Hubbard finished with 12 points on 4-of-15 shooting. Bowen led Penn State with 18, and Ivan Jurić scored 15 points and pulled down 17 rebounds. It was Jurić’s eighth straight double-double, breaking the Penn State record set by John Amaechi in 1994–95. The Bulldogs leave the Bahamas at 5–3. They return to Humphrey Coliseum in Starkville to face Georgia Tech on Wednesday, Dec. 2, at 8:15 p.m. Central.
